page.layout: One page of text, printed page number 144 at top left, running head "EMBLEMATA ET" at top centre. Main text in one column. Right margin shows show-through and faint marks; left margin holds a handwritten annotation (manuscript, not printed) and a large manuscript flourish at the foot, which are not transcribed.

main_text.l: Tantus amor nobis humanas fingere voces,
Totus in hoc vt sit nocte diéque labor.
Quòd si forte negat volucrum mihi Pallas apisc-
iQuod cupio, tantus me capit inde dolor,
Protinus vt vitæ lucem sit linquere dulce,
Et gratum mortis iam mihi pondus eat.
Inunc, & picas linguâ infectare loquaces:
Discendi studium fac imitere tamen.
Monetarum & aetatum comparatio.
Prisca moneta fuit meliori facta metallo:
Deteriore sed est commate cusa nouo.
Illi priscorum soleo contendere mores.
Isti sed mores confero sæpe nouos.
Gallica certamina.
Acrior ad pugnam fieret quò Græca iuuentus,
Pugnaces Gallos sueta videre fuit.
At si quis videat, quas miscet Gallia, pugnas,(
Tota quibus miseræ vah! laniata perit.)
Exuerit si non hominem, mala nomina belli-
Horrescens, placidæ pacis amator erit.
Ex obscuro splendidus.
Est in equis patrum virtus plerumque repofita:
Atque refert ortum stirps generosa suum.
Nonnunquam tamen ex imbellis stirpe caballi,
Elide qui currat victor, abibit equus.
Sic quanquam fortes oriantur fortibus: heros-
Omnis ab heroum non trahit arce genus.
Nascitur ex vena mediocri sæpe creatus,
Cui natura dedit robur & ingenium.

page.notes: Manuscript annotations in the left margin and at the foot (a handwritten "Nimis" and a flourish) are not printed text and are omitted. Faint show-through from the reverse page appears in the right margin. Lines 4 and 6 of the second section are set in italics in the original; the heading "Monetarum & aetatum comparatio" carries a manuscript cross mark. The line "Nimia" at the lower right is a partly cut manuscript word.
